newsitem.title: USA: Harvard hires firm to help sell unit.
newsitem.headline: Harvard hires firm to help sell unit.

text.p: Harvard Industries Inc said Monday it has hired the investment banking firm of Houlihan Lokey Howard & Zukin to assist it in selling its Doehler-Jarvis subsidiary.

Harvard Industries described the unit it plans to sell as the largest independent manufacturer of aluminum castings in North America. Houlihan Lokey will immediately begin soliciting offers for Doehler-Jarvis, it said.

"Harvard is committed to completing the sale of Doehler-Jarvis on an expedited basis in order to help facilitate our reorganization under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code...," said John W. Adams, Harvard's chairman.

Harvard said Doehler-Jarvis' revenues for fiscal year ended September 30, 1996, were approximately $296 million. It operates facilities in Toledo, Ohio, Greeneville, Tenn., and Pottstown, Pa., and employs approximately 2,000, it said.
Harvard said it expects to seek bankruptcy court approval for the highest and best offer that is obtained within 60 days.
Harvard, through its subsidiaries, designs, develops and manufactures a broad range of components for original equipment manufacturers, producing cars and light trucks in North America and abroad.
The company and its nine affiliates, incluiding Doehler-Jarvis filed for bankruptcy protection from creditors on May 8.
